# `silk/url/host`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Parse and serialize the host of a URL as the WHATWG URL Standard specifies: domains, IPv4 and
IPv6 addresses, and opaque hosts.

## When to use
Use [`UrlHost.parse`](#UrlHost.impl.parse) to check and normalize a host name outside a full URL, such as the
`Host` of a request. `silk.url.url` calls it for every URL.

## Details
A host of a special URL, such as `http`, is percent-decoded and converted with UTS #46 (see
`silk.text.idna`). A domain that ends in a number is an IPv4 address, which can be written in
decimal, octal, or hexadecimal parts. A host in brackets is an IPv6 address. The host of a
URL that is not special is opaque: it is only checked and percent-encoded.

## Examples
### Normalize hosts
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.url.host { UrlHost, UrlHostKind }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut output = Bytes.make()
  let kind = run UrlHost.parse(b"0x7f.1", false, &mut output)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let ipv4 = match kind {
    Option<UrlHostKind>.Some { value } => value == UrlHostKind.Ipv4
    Option<UrlHostKind>.None => false
  }
  if !ipv4 || Bytes.asSlice(&output) != b"127.0.0.1" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `UrlHost` with `import silk.url.host { UrlHost }`.

<a id="UrlHost.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(input: &[u8], opaque: bool, output: &mut Bytes) -> Option<UrlHostKind>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `input` as the host of a URL and appends its serialization to `output`. Returns the
kind of the host, or `None` if `input` is not a valid host.

#### Details
`opaque` is `true` for the host of a URL that is not special. Then `input` is checked for
forbidden host code points and percent-encoded, unless it is an IPv6 address in brackets.
Otherwise `input` is percent-decoded, converted to ASCII, and read as an IPv4 address when it
ends in a number. An empty `input` gives `Empty` only when `opaque` is `true`. On failure,
`output` can hold a part of the result.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="UrlHost.impl.domainToAscii"></a>

### Associated function `domainToAscii`

```silk
pub effect fn domainToAscii(domain: string, output: &mut Bytes) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Converts `domain` to ASCII as the URL Standard's domain to ASCII does, and appends it to
`output`. Returns `false` if `domain` is not a valid domain.

#### Details
ASCII input is only lowercased. Other input goes through UTS #46 ToASCII with the bidi and
joiner checks. An empty result, or one with a forbidden domain code point, is not valid. On
failure, `output` can hold a part of the result.

#### Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.
